title: Option to Result
story: You're connecting two libraries. One returns Option (found it or not), but your code needs Result (it worked or here's why). You need a bridge between the two worlds — and you can build it with match.
why: Option and Result are interchangeable with a simple conversion — turning None into Err gives you error messages, turning Err into None discards details when unnecessary.
analogy: Converting Option to Result is like upgrading from a 'yes/no' signal to a full explanation — Option says 'nothing there,' Result says 'nothing there BECAUSE the database was offline.'
try_it: Write a bi-directional pipeline: start with Option, convert to Result, transform inside Result, convert back to Option. Use it to look up a config value, validate it, then return Some(validated) or None if anything fails.
tips: Convert Option to Result when you need to attach an error message to a missing value
Convert Result to Option when the caller doesn't care WHY something failed, just whether it did
The conversion functions are just match statements — write them once and reuse them
common_mistakes: Converting `Some(error_msg)` to `Err(error_msg)` — Some means success in Option world, Ok means success in Result world
Losing important error info by converting Result to Option too early — keep the error until you're sure you don't need it
Writing the conversion inside every function instead of making a reusable helper
